summary: Local-first Chrome extension that scrolls through a complete web page, stabilizes changing presentation, stitches captured frames in the browser, and opens one reusable PNG.
scope: Capture lifecycle, page stabilization, local image processing, and release delivery
problem: Chrome's standard screenshot flow captures only the visible viewport, while many full-page tools add accounts, editors, or cloud upload to a job that should produce one complete local image.
constraints: Chrome can capture only the active visible tab, so the source tab must stay active while 1Snap scrolls and records each frame.
Dynamic content, visible images and fonts, fixed or sticky elements, and the user's original scroll position must be stabilized or restored without leaving the page altered.
Captures are bounded to 50 frames, 16,000 by 32,000 output dimensions, and 120 million pixels, with proportional downscaling when needed.

Built IndexedDB frame retention, local Canvas stitching, output sizing safeguards, and the measured result page.
Established unit and UI coverage, the product website, Netlify deployment, and checksummed Manifest V3 release packaging.
outcomes: Users can turn a regular web page into one full-height PNG from a single toolbar action.
Capture frames and image assembly remain inside extension-owned browser storage and processing.
The result page exposes dimensions, file size, source, time, frame count, copy, and download actions.
Maintainers can ship and verify a versioned Chrome ZIP with a matching SHA-256 checksum.

summary: A production-oriented publishing workspace that moves one idea through generation, brand controls, platform preview, and scheduled delivery.
scope: AI workflow, publishing integrations, and background jobs
problem: Creators and small teams repeat the same editorial work for every social platform. They rewrite one idea for different limits, compare weak AI variants, check brand language, and then move the result into separate publishing tools.
constraints: AI providers vary in availability, rate limits, model behavior, and key quotas.
LinkedIn, X, and Facebook each impose different OAuth, account, content, and API requirements.
Scheduled publishing must survive beyond the request that created it and retain a reviewable status.

architecture.summary: The Next.js application keeps HTTP boundaries in route handlers, product logic in domain modules, infrastructure in core services, and durable delivery in Inngest.

summary: Check if your Bangladesh TIN is selected for NBR Risk-Based Audit (AY 2023-24). Client-side, private, instant lookup of 72,342 returns.
role: Data modeling, validation, and release engineering
scope: Provenance, transformation, validation, and distribution
problem: A static historical audit list is inconvenient to search manually, especially on mobile, while submitting a tax identifier to another application server creates avoidable query exposure.
constraints: The data is historical, not live audit/compliance status.
Claimed NBR provenance, accuracy, completeness, and redistribution rights are not established.
Shipping the dataset to browsers makes records retrievable even though lookup queries stay client-side.
